questions.q: Along the $x$-axis, three charges $\frac{q}{2},-q$ and $\frac{q}{2}$ are placed at $x=0, x=a$ and $x=2 a$ respectively. The resultant electric potential at a point $P$ located at a distance $r$ from the charge $-q(a < r)$ is \left(\varepsilon_0\right.$ is the permittivity of free space)$
questions.solution:
As $r \gg a$, so $r>2 a$ So, potential at point $P$
$\begin{aligned} V & =\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}\left[\frac{q / 2}{r+a}-\frac{q}{r}+\frac{q / 2}{r-a}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q}{2}\left[\frac{1}{r+a}-\frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{r-a}\right] \\ & =\frac{q}{8 \pi \varepsilon_0}\left[\frac{r(r-a)-2\left(r^2-a^2\right)+r(r+a)}{r\left(r^2-a^2\right)}\right] \\ & =\frac{q}{8 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{2 a^2}{r\left(r^2-a^2\right)} \\ & =\frac{q a^2}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 r^3}(\text { as } r>a)\end{aligned}$
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: A neutral sphere of radius $r$ and density $ρ$ is placed in a uniform electric field $E$ that exists on the earth's surface in the vertically upward direction. If the atomic number and the mass number of the material of the sphere are $Z$ and $A$ respectively, then the fraction of electrons that should be removed from the sphere for it to remain in equilibrium is [Assume that the sphere is able to hold the necessary charge without any leakage. Here ${N}_{A}$ -- Avogadro number]
questions.solution:
Let us assume that we remove $n$ electrons from the sphere due to which the net charge on the sphere is $q = ne$

For the sphere to be in equilibrium

$mg = qE = neE$

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}ρg = neE$

$⇒ n = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρg}{3eE}$
The number of moles of the metal in the sphere is

${n}_{mol} = \dfrac{m}{A} = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρ}{3A}$

So the number of metal atoms will be

${n}_{metalatoms} = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρ}{3A} \times {N}_{A}$

This means the total number of electrons in the sphere is

${n}_{total} = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρ{N}_{A}}{3A} \times Z$

Hence, the fraction is

$\dfrac{n}{ntotal} = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρg}{3eE} \times \dfrac{3A}{4\pir^{3}ρ{N}_{A}Z}$

$⇒ \dfrac{n}{ntotal} = \dfrac{gA}{eE{N}_{A}Z}$

questions.q: A body of mass $1 \mathrm{~g}$ and carrying a charge $10^{-8} \mathrm{C}$ passes from two points $P$ and $Q . P$ and $Q$ are at electric potentials. $600 \mathrm{~V}$ and $0 \mathrm{~V}$, respectively. The velocity of the body at $Q$ is $20 \mathrm{cms}^{-1}$. It velocity in $\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ at $P$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}$m & =1 $\mathrm{~g}=$10^{-3} $\mathrm{~kg},$\\
v & =20 $\mathrm{~cm}$/ $\mathrm{s}=$20 $\times$10^{-20} $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}$\\
q & =10^{-8} $\mathrm{C}$\\
V_p & =600 $\mathrm{volt}$\\
V_Q & =0 $\text { volt }
\end{aligned}$Work done in moving the charge from $P$ to $Q\begin{aligned}$W & =q V_{P Q}=10^{-8}(600-0) \\
& =600 $\times$10^{-8} $\mathrm{~J}
\end{aligned}$From work energy theorem
Work done $=$ change in $\mathrm{KE}\begin{aligned}$600 $\times$10^{-8} & =$\frac{1}{2}$m\left($20 $\times$10^{-2}\right)^2-$\frac{1}{2}$m v² \\
600 $\times$10^{-8} & =$\frac{1}{2} \times$10^{-3} $\times$4 $\times$10^{-2}-$\frac{1}{2} \times$10^{-3} $\times$v^2 \\
$\frac{1}{2} \times$10^{-3} $\times$v^2 & =2 $\times$10^{-5}-600 $\times$10^{-8} \\
& =2 $\times$10^{-5}-0.6 $\times$10^{-5} \\
v² & =1.4 $\times$10^{-2} $\times$2=28 $\times$10^{-2} \\
v & =$\sqrt{28 \times 10^{-2}}=\sqrt{0.028} \mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}

questions.q: Two small conducting balls of identical mass $20 \mathrm{~g}$ and identical charge $10^{-10} \mathrm{C}$ hang from non-conducting threads of length, $L=300 \mathrm{~cm}$. If the equilibrium separation of balls is $x$ and $x \ll L$ then the magnitude of $x$ is (Assume, $4 \pi \in_0=\frac{1}{9 \times 10^9} \mathrm{~F} / \mathrm{m}$ and $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.solution:
Given, mass of each spherical ball, m=20 $\mathrm{~g}=$2 $\times$10^{-2} $\mathrm{~kg},$g=10 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^2 charge on each spherical ball, q_1=q_2=q=10^{-10} $\mathrm{C}$and length of thread, L=300 $\mathrm{~cm}=$3 $\mathrm{~m}$According to the question,
Equilibrium at point $B$, $\begin{aligned}$T \cos $\theta$ \text{ and } =m g \\ T \sin $\theta$ \text{ and } =F \\ T \sin $\theta$ \text{ and } =$\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q^2}{x^2} \end{aligned} ($From Coulomb's law) From Eqn. (i) and (ii), we get $\frac{T \sin \theta}{T \cos \theta}=\frac{\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q^2}{x^2}}{m g} \left[\text { Given, }$4 $\pi \varepsilon_0=\frac{1}{9 \times 10^9} \mathrm{C}^2$/ $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m}^2\right]\therefore m g \tan \theta=9 \times10^9 \cdot \frac{q^2}{x^2}$From $\triangle A B M$, $\tan \theta=\frac{\frac{x}{2}}{\sqrt{L^2-\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^2}}=\frac{x}{\sqrt{4 L^2-x^2}}=\frac{x}{2 L} \quad(\becauseL>x)\therefore$ From Eq. (iii), we get m g $\cdot \frac{x}{2 L}=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times q^2}{x^2}$Putting the given values, we get $\begin{array}{rlrl}$2 $\times$10^{-2} $\times$10 $\times \frac{x}{2 \times 3}$ \text{ and } $=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 10^{-20}}{x^2}$\\ \Rightarrow \quad x³ \text{ and } $=\frac{27}{10^{10}} \mathrm{~m}$\\ \Rightarrow \quad x \text{ and } \quad $\frac{3}{10^3 \times 10^{1 / 3}}$ \text{ and } $=\frac{3}{10^{1 / 3}} \mathrm{~mm} \end{array}$Therefore, magnitude of equilibrium separation distance of balls is $\frac{3}{10^{1 / 3}} \mathrm{~mm}.

The line $AA '$ is on a charged infinite conducting plane which is perpendicular to the plane of the paper. The plane has a surface density of charge $\sigma$ and $B$ is a ball of mass $m$ with a like charge of magnitude $q$. $B$ is connected by a string from a point on the line $AA '$. The tangent of the angle \left(\theta\right)$ formed between the line $AA '$ and the string is (provided, the charge $q$ does not affect the distribution of charge on conducting plate)

$
questions.solution:
The diagram is as follows,



The electric filed due to charged infinite conducting sheet is $E = \dfrac{σ}{ε0}$

Now, force (electric force) on the charged ball is $F = qE = \dfrac{\sigma \cdot q}{ε0}$

The resultant of electric force and $mg$ balance the tension produced in the string.

So, $tan \theta = \dfrac{Fe}{mg} = \dfrac{qσ}{{ε}_{0}mg} = \dfrac{qσ}{{ε}_{0}mg}$

questions.q: Two uniformly charged nonconducting spheres, each of radius $R$, are fixed in a gravity free space as shown in the figure. If an electron is released at rest from the point $A$, then its speed just before striking the other sphere is $[$mass of electron = ${m}_{e} ]$
questions.solution:
Using the conservation of mechanical energy, we get

$\dfrac{KQe}{R} - \dfrac{KQe}{9R} = \dfrac{-KQe}{R} + \dfrac{KQe}{9\text{R}} + \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2}$

$- \dfrac{2\text{KQe}}{9\text{R}} + \dfrac{2\text{KQe}}{R} = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2}$

$\dfrac{16}{4{πε}_{0}}\dfrac{eQ}{9\text{R}} = \dfrac{1}{2}{mv}^{2} ⇒ \text{v} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8Qe}{9{πε}_{0}{m}_{e}R}}$

questions.solution:
Force on ( $- {q}_{1}$ ) due to ${q}_{2} = \dfrac{{q}_{1} {q}_{2}}{4\pi{ε}_{0} b^{2}}$

$∴{F}_{1} = \dfrac{{q}_{1} {q}_{2}}{4 \pi {ε}_{0} b^{2}}$ along \left({q}_{1} {q}_{2}\right)$

$\text{Force on} \left(- {q}_{1}\right) \text{due to} \left({- \text{q}}_{3}\right)= \dfrac{{( \text{q}}_{1} {) ( \text{q}}_{3} )}{4 \pi {ε}_{0} a^{2}}$

${F}_{2} = \dfrac{{q}_{1} {q}_{3}}{4 \pi {ε}_{0} a^{2}}$ as shown

${F}_{2}$> makes an angle of \left({90}^{0} - \theta\right)$ with \left({q}_{1} {q}_{2}\right)$



Resolved part of ${F}_{2}$ along ${q}_{1} {q}_{2}$

$= {F}_{2} cos \left({90}^{0} - \theta\right)

$= $\dfrac{{q}_{1} {q}_{3} \text\sin \theta}{4 \pi {ε}_{0} a^{2}} along \left({q}_{1} {q}_{2}\right)

$∴$ Total force on \left(- {q}_{1}\right)

$= [ $\dfrac{{q}_{1} {q}_{2}}{4 \pi {ε}_{0} b^{2}} + \dfrac{{q}_{1} {q}_{3} \text\sin \theta}{4 \pi {ε}_{0} a^{2}} ]along x-axis

$∴$ x-component of force $∝ [ \dfrac{{q}_{2}}{b^{2}} + \dfrac{{q}_{3}}{a^{2}} \text\sin \theta ].$

questions.q: A conducting soap bubble having a radius $a,$ thickness $t  \left(< < a\right)$ is charged to a potential $V. If now, the bubble collapses and forms a droplet, then the potential of the droplet is$
questions.solution:
Let q be the charge on the bubble, then

$\text{V} = \dfrac{\text{Kq}}{\text{a}}$ (Here $\text{K} = \dfrac{1}{4 \pi {ε}_{0}}$ )

$∴ \text{q} = \dfrac{\text{Va}}{\text{K}}$

Let after collapsing, the radius of droplet becomes R, then equating the volume, we have

\left(4 \pi a^{2}\right) \text{t} = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^{3}$

$∴ \text{R} = {\left(3 a^{2} \text{t}\right)}^{1 / 3}$

Now, potential of droplet will be

$V^{′} = \dfrac{\text{Kq}}{\text{R}}$

Substituting the values, we have

$V^{′} = \dfrac{\left(\text{K}\right) \left(\dfrac{\text{Va}}{\text{K}}\right)}{{\left(3 a^{2} \text{t}\right)}^{1 / 3}}$

or $V^{′} = \text{V} {\left(\dfrac{\text{a}}{3 \text{t}}\right)}^{1 / 3}

questions.q: Three identical charges, each $2 \mu \mathrm{C}$ lie at the vertices of a right angled triangle as shown in the figure. Forces on the charge at $B$ due to the charges at $A$ and $C$ respectively are $F_1$ and $F_2$. The angle between their resultant force and $F_2$ is
questions.solution:
From figure the net force $F_{\text {net }}$ due to $F_1$ and $F_2$ makes an angle $\theta$ with force $\mathrm{F}_2$
$\begin{aligned} & \tan \theta=\frac{\mathrm{F}_1}{\mathrm{~F}_2} \\ & \text { Also, } \mathrm{F}_1=k \cdot \frac{q_1 q_2}{(3)^2} \\ & \because \quad q_1=q_2=q_3=2 \mu \mathrm{C} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{F}_2=k \cdot \frac{q_1 q_3}{(4)^3} \\ & \therefore \quad \tan \theta=k \cdot \frac{q_1 q_2 /(3)^2}{q_1 q_3 /(4)^2}=\frac{(4)^2}{(3)^2}=\frac{16}{9} \\ & \therefore \quad \theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{16}{9}\right) \end{aligned}$

questions.q: An infinite number of electric charges each equal to 5 nano-coulomb (magnitude) are placed along $X$-axis at $x=1 \mathrm{~cm}, x=2 \mathrm{~cm}$, $x=4 \mathrm{~cm}, x=8 \mathrm{~cm} . . .$. and so on. In this set up if the consecutive charges have opposite sign, then the electric field in newton/coulomb at $x=0$ is :  \left(\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}=9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{~N}-\mathrm{m}^2 / \mathrm{C}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
Electric field intensity due to a point charge. $E=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{Q}{r^2}$
The consecutive charges are of opposite signs. $\therefore$ Net electric field at $x=0$, is $E=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}\left[\frac{Q}{r_1^2}-\frac{Q}{r_2^2}+\frac{Q}{r_3^2}-\frac{Q}{r_4^2} \ldots . . \infty\right]=\frac{Q}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}\left[\frac{1}{r_1^2}-\frac{1}{r_2^2}+\frac{1}{r_3^2}-\frac{1}{r_4^2}+\ldots . \infty\right\rceil=9 \times 10^9 \times 5 \times 10^{-9}\left[\frac{1}{\left(1 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2}-\frac{1}{\left(2 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2}+\frac{1}{\left(4 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2}+\ldots \infty\right\rfloor=\frac{45}{10^{-4}}\left[\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}+\frac{1}{4^2}-\frac{1}{8^2}+\ldots . \infty\right]=45 \times 10^4\left[\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}+\frac{1}{4^2}-\frac{1}{8^2} \ldots \infty\right]\left\lceil\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}+\frac{1}{4^2}-\frac{1}{8^2} \ldots \infty\right\rfloor=\frac{\frac{1}{1^2}}{1-\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)^2}\left[\right.$ Sum of infinite GP, \left.\mathrm{S}_{\infty}=\frac{a}{1-r}\right]=\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{4}{5}\therefore \quad E=45 \times 10^4 \times \frac{4}{5}=36 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{C}

questions.q: An electric dipole is placed at the origin and is directed along the $x$-axis. At a point $P$, far away from the dipole, the electric field is parallel to the $y$-axis. $OP$ makes an angle $\theta$ with the $x$-axis, then
questions.solution:
Direction of the electric field from the axis of the dipole is given by $= \theta + \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{\text\tan \theta}{2}\right)

Here given that E is along the $y$-axis.

\theta + \tan^{- 1} \left(\dfrac{\text\tan \theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}



\dfrac{\text\tan \theta}{2} = \text\cot \theta

\text\tan \theta =$2 cot $\theta$⇒ \tan^{2} $\theta =$2$

$∴ \text\tan \theta = \sqrt{2}

questions.q: Three identical metal plates with large surface areas are kept parallel to each other as shown in the figure. The leftmost plate is given a charge $Q$, the rightmost a charge $- 2Q$ and the middle one remains neutral. Find the charge appearing on the outer surface of the rightmost plate.
questions.solution:
Let the charge distribution on the plates is as shown in the figure.

Electric field due to a charged& surface& having area& $A$~and ~carrying charge~$q$~is~

$E = \dfrac{q}{2A{ε}_{0}}$

Let's consider right direction to be positive and left direction to be negative.

We know that electric field inside a conductor or metal is zero. Hence, equating electric field at point~$P$~inside the right most plate as zero.

$\dfrac{Q + X}{2A{ε}_{O}} + \dfrac{X}{2A{ε}_{O}} - \dfrac{X}{2A{ε}_{O}} + \dfrac{X}{2A{ε}_{O}} - \dfrac{X}{2A{ε}_{O}} + \left(\dfrac{2Q + X}{2A{ε}_{O}}\right) = 0$

$\dfrac{Q + X}{2A{ε}_{O}} + \left(\dfrac{2Q + X}{2A{ε}_{O}}\right) = 0$

$3Q + 2X = 0$

$X = \dfrac{- 3Q}{2}$

$∴$ Charge on outer surface of leftmost plate is

$= - X - 2Q$

$= \dfrac{3Q}{2} - 2Q$

$= \dfrac{- Q}{2}$

questions.q: Two charged identical metal spheres $A$ and $B$ repel each other with a force of $3 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~N}$. Another identical wncharged sphere $C$ is touched with sphere $A$ and then it is placed mid-way between $A$ and $B$. Then, the magnitude of net force on $C$ is
questions.solution:
Spheres $A$ and $B$ have the same charge of same nature. When uncharged sphere $C$ is touched with sphere $A$, then charge is transferred to $C$ and this charge is equally divided between two spheres.
Let initially the charge on spheres $A$ and $B$ is $q$. Initially, the repelling force between charged spheres $A$ and $B=3 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~N}$ When, sphere $C$, is placed between charged spheres $A$ and $B$, then the force between $A$ and $C$, F_{A C}=$\frac{k \frac{q}{2} \times q / 2}{(r / 2)^2}$Similarly, between $B$ and $C$ F_{B C}=$\frac{k q \times q / 2}{(r / 2)^2}$The magnitude of net force on $C, F^{\prime}=F_{B C}-F_{A C}$ Also F=$\frac{k q \times q}{r^2}=$3 $\times$10^{-5} $\mathrm{~N}$So, $\frac{F}{F_{B C}-F_{A C}}=\frac{\left(k q^2 / r^2\right)}{k\left[\frac{q \times q / 2}{(r / 2)^2}-\frac{q / 2 \times q / 2}{(r / 2)^2}\right]}$ Here, $\quad F=3 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~N}, F_{B C}-F_{A C}=F^{\prime}\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{3 \times 10^{-5}}{F^{\prime}}$& =$\frac{1}{2-1}=\frac{1}{1}=$1 \\ \therefore \quad & F^{\prime} & =3 $\times$10^{-5} $\mathrm{~N} \end{aligned}$

In air, a charged soap bubble of radius& $r$~is in equilibrium, outside and inside pressures being equal. The charge on the drop is \left(\varepsilon_{0}=\right.$ permittivity of free space, $T=$ surface tension of soap solution),

$
questions.solution:
For a charged soap bubble&

${P}_{external} + {P}_{electric} = \dfrac{4T}{r}$

We also know that electrostatic pressure on the patch(small part of the charged surface)~

$ElectrostaticPressure = \dfrac{\sigma2}{2{ε}_{0}}$

In equilibrium condition, equating above equations

$\dfrac{\sigma2}{2{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{4T}{r}$

${σ}^{2} = \dfrac{8{ε}_{0}T}{r}$

$⇒ \sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{8{ε}_{0}T}{r}}$~ ~ \left[\sigma = \dfrac{Q}{A}, whereAissurfaceareaofsphericalsoapbubble .\right]$

$⇒ \dfrac{Q}{4\pir^{2}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{8{ε}_{0}T}{r}}$

$⇒ Q = 4\pir^{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{8{ε}_{0}T}{r}}$

$

questions.q: A charge $( - q, m )$~is projected with an initial velocity ${v}_{0}$~in the direction of a unidirectional field ${E}_{0}x$& as shown in the figure. Find the distance covered by the charge before it& comes to rest.
questions.solution:
Since the charge& is negative and is projected along the electric field, it will experience a retardation& $\dfrac{q{E}_{0}}{m}$.

Let~the charge travel~a distance $s$~before coming to rest $( v = 0 )$. Using the third equation of motion,

$v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$

$u^{2} = - 2as$

$⇒ {v0}^{2} = \dfrac{2q{E}_{0}s}{m}$

$⇒ s = {v}_{0}\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{2q{E}_{0}}}$.

questions.q: Two charge metallic spheres are joined by a very thin metal wire. If the radius of the larger sphere is four times that of the smaller sphere, the electric field near the larger sphere is
options: twice that near the smaller sphere
quarter of that near the smaller sphere
same as that near the smaller sphere
half of that near smaller sphere
questions.solution: Since the spheres are joined by a metal wire, their potentials will be same. Let the radius of the smaller sphere be $r_1$ and the radius of the larger sphere be $r_2=4 r_1$ the $\mathrm{v}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{q}_1}{\mathrm{r}_1}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{q}_2}{\mathrm{r}_2}$ \therefore $\frac{\mathrm{q}_2}{\mathrm{q}_1}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_2}{\mathrm{r}_1}$The electric field near the surface of spheres are given by $\begin{aligned}$& $\mathrm{E}}_{1}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{q}_1}{\mathrm{r}_1^2} \text { and } \mathrm{E}}_{2}=$\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{q}_2}{\mathrm{r}_2^2}$\\  \text{ and }  \therefore $\frac{\mathrm{E}_2}{\mathrm{E}_1}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_2}{\mathrm{q}_1} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{r}_1^2}{\mathrm{r}_2^2}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_2}{\mathrm{r}_1} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{r}_1^2}{\mathrm{r}_2^2}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_1}{\mathrm{r}_2}=\frac{1}{4} \end{aligned}

questions.q: A simple pendulum with a bob of mass $40 \mathrm{~g}$ and charge $+2 \mu \mathrm{C}$ makes 20 oscillation in $44 \mathrm{~s}$. A vertical electric field magnitude $4.2 \times 10^4 \mathrm{NC}^{-1}$ pointing downward is applied. The time taken by the pendulum to make 15 oscillation in the electric field is (acceleration due to gravity $=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$ )
questions.solution: Mass, $m=40 \mathrm{~g}=0.04 \mathrm{~kg}, q=2 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{C}$ Now, $\quad m a=q E\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad$a & =$\frac{q}{m}$E \\ & =$\frac{2 \times 10^{-6}}{0.04} \times$4.2 $\times$10^4 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^2 \\  \text{ and }  =2.1 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^2($\text { downward }) \end{aligned}$So, effective acceleration on bob, a_e=a+g=12.1 $\mathrm{~m}$/ $\mathrm{s}^2 In the absence of electric field, T=2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}=$2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{10}}$In the presence of electric field, $\begin{aligned}$T^{\prime}  \text{ and }  =2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{a_e}}=$2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{12.1}}$\\ $\frac{T}{T^{\prime}}$ \text{ and }  =$\sqrt{\frac{12.1}{10}}=\frac{11}{10} \Rightarrow$T^{\prime}=$\frac{10}{11}$T \end{aligned} Given, $\quad T=\frac{44}{20} \Rightarrow T^{\prime}=\frac{10}{11} \times \frac{44}{20}=2 \mathrm{~s}$ So, time taken in 15 oscillations =2 $\times$15=30 $\mathrm{~s}

questions.q: An inclined plane making an angle \(30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\) with the horizontal is placed in a uniform horizontal electric field of \(100 $\mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$\) as shown in the figure. A small block of mass \($\mathrm{I} \mathrm{kg}$\) and charge, 0.01C is allowed to slide down from rest from a height, \(h=1 $\mathrm{~m}$\). If the coefficient of friction is 0.2 , then the acceleration of the block is nearly, (Acceleration due to gravity, \(g=10 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$\) )
questions.solution:
According to the question, an inclined plane is making an angle of \(30^{\circ}\) with the horizontal, placed in a uniform electric field of \(100 $\mathrm{~nm}^{-1}$\). It can be such in the figure that a block of mass \(m\) is sliding down from rest at height \(h\).
From the above diagram, the total force \(F\) acting along inclined plane. From fig, \(m g \sin 30^{\circ}-\mu m g \cos 30^{\circ}-q E \cos 30^{\circ}=m a=F\) Given, \(\mu=0.2, m=1 $\mathrm{~kg},,$q=0.01 $\mathrm{C}$\) and \(h=1 $\mathrm{~m}$\) Putting these values, we get \(\begin{aligned} & 10 \times $\frac{1}{2}-$0.2 \times 10 \times $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-$0.01 \times 100 \times $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=$a \\ & $a=5-\sqrt{3}-$0.5 $\sqrt{3} \approx$2.3 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-2} \end{aligned}$\) Hence, the acceleration of the block is nearly, \(2.3 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-2}$\).

questions.q: A hollow cylinder has a charge $\text{q}$ coulomb within it. If $ϕ$ is the electric flux in units of $\text{Vm}$ associated with the curved surface $\text{B}$, the flux linked with the plane surface $\text{A}$ in units of $\text{Vm}$ will be
questions.solution:
Let ${ϕ}_{A} \text{,} {ϕ}_{B} \text{and} {ϕ}_{C}$ are the electric flux linked with $\text{A}, \text{B}\text{and C}$.

According to gauss theorem, $ϕ$ total $= \dfrac{∑ q}{{ε}_{0}}$

${ϕ}_{A} + {ϕ}_{B} + {ϕ}_{C} = \dfrac{\text{q}}{{ε}_{0}}$

Since ${ϕ}_{A} = {ϕ}_{C} \text{,}$

$∴ 2 {ϕ}_{A} + {ϕ}_{B} = \dfrac{\text{q}}{{ε}_{0}}$

or $2 {ϕ}_{A} = \dfrac{\text{q}}{{ε}_{0}} - {ϕ}_{B}$

or $2 {ϕ}_{A} = \dfrac{\text{q}}{{ε}_{0}} - ϕ$

(Given ${ϕ}_{B} = ϕ$)

$∴ {ϕ}_{A} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{\text{q}}{{ε}_{0}} -ϕ\right)$

questions.q: A proton, a deutron and an $\alpha$-particle having the same momentum, enters a region of uniform electric field between the parallel plates of a capacitor. The electric field is perpendicular to the initial path of the particles. Then the ratio of deflections suffered by them is
questions.solution:
The deflection suffered by charged particle in an electric field is
$y=\frac{q E L D}{m \mu^2}=\frac{q E L D}{p^2 / m} \quad(p=m u)\Rightarrow \quad y \propto \frac{q m}{p^2}\Rightarrow y_p: y_d: y_\alpha=\frac{q_p m_p}{p_p^2}: \frac{q_d m_d}{p_d^2}: \frac{q_\alpha m_\alpha}{p_a^2}$
Since, $\quad p_\alpha=p_d=p_p \quad$ (given)
$m_p: m_d: m_\alpha=1: 2: 4$
and $\quad q_1: q_d: q_\alpha=1: 1: 2\Rightarrow \quad y_b: y_d: y_\alpha=1 \times 1: 1 \times 2: 2 \times 4=1: 2: 8$

questions.q: An electric dipole consists of two particle each of mass $1 \mathrm{~kg}$ separated by $\mathrm{l} \mathrm{m}$ carrying charges $1 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and $-1 \mu \mathrm{C}$ respectively. It is in equilibrium in a uniform electric field of $2 \times 10^4 \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}$. If it is deflected by a small angle $2^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$, minimum time taken by it to come back again to the mean position is (in seconds)
questions.solution: Torque on dipole, when it is deflected by a small angle $\theta$ is $\tau=p E \sin \theta=p E \theta$ \{ for small angle, $\sin \theta=\theta\}$ But $\quad \tau=I \alpha$ where, $\quad I=m r^2+m r^2=2 m r^2$ So, angular acceleration of dipole is $\alpha=\frac{p E \theta}{I}$Time to align back with field is  \left(\right.$ using \left.\theta=\frac{1}{2} \alpha t^2\right)$ t=$\sqrt{\frac{2 \theta}{\alpha}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 \theta I}{p E \theta}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 I}{P E}}=\sqrt{50} \approx$2 $\cdot$5 $\pi(\mathrm{s})$

questions.q: A uniformly charged spherical shell of radius& $R$ carries a uniform~charge density of~$\sigma$ per unit area. It is made of two hemispherical shells, held together by pressing them with force~$F$.~$F$& is proportional to&
questions.solution:
The electrostatic pressure at a point on the charged conducting surface of surface charge density& $\sigma$~is~$\dfrac{d F}{d A} = \dfrac{\sigma2}{2{ε}_{0}}$

Due to the electrostatic repulsion between the charged hemisphere, there is a requirement of an external force~$F$~on each hemisphere which will balance the electrostatic force due to the~other hemisphere.

For the given case, consider a thin ring at an angle~$\theta$~away from the diametrical axis. Now lets take a small ring of angle~$d \theta$~around this ring, as shown in the figure below~:

Let~$d A$~be the area element corresponding to the small ring such that~$d A = \left[2\pi \left(Rsin \theta\right)\right] \times \l$lleft(Rd\theta\right)

Now due to the electrostatic force,~there will be an electrostatic pressure on the whole sphere. For the small ring~$d F = \dfrac{\sigma2}{2{ε}_{0}} \timesdA$

Component of~$d F$~along vertical axis will be~$d Fcos \left(\theta\right).$By symmetry, all horizontal components will cancel each other.

Therefore, total force :

$F = {∫}_{0}^{\pi2} d Fcos\theta⇒ F = {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\dfrac{\sigma2}{2{ε}_{0}}$2\piR^{2}sin \thetacos\thetad $\theta

$⇒ F = {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\dfrac{\sigma2}{2{ε}_{0}}\p$piR^{2}sin\lleft(2\theta\right)d \theta$

$⇒ F = $\dfrac{\sigma2}{2{ε}_{0}}\piR^{2}{\dfrac{- cos\left(2\theta\right)}{2}}_{0}^{\pi2}

$⇒ F = $\dfrac{\sigma2}{2{ε}_{0}}\piR^{2}

$⇒ F ∝ $\dfrac{\sigma2}{ε0}$R^{2}$

questions.q: Two charged particles each of mass $9.8 \mathrm{~g}$ and charges $+20 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and $-20 \mu \mathrm{C}$ are attached to the two ends of a massless and rigid uniform non-conducting rod of length $50 \mathrm{~cm}$. This arrangement is held in a uniform electric field of $12.1 \mathrm{NC}^{-1}$, such that the rod makes a very small angle with the field direction. If the rod is set free, the minimum time needed for the rod to become parallel to the direction of the electric field is ................ seconds.
questions.solution: This arrangement of electric dipole in electric field will undergo SHM, when the rod is set free. Time period of this SHM is given by T=2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{I}{\mathrm{PE}}}$where, $I=$ moment of inertia of dipole, $p=$ electric dipole moment and $E=$ electric field. $I=2 m r^2\begin{aligned}$& $\text { mass, }$m=9.8 $\times$10^{-3} $\mathrm{~kg},$r=$\frac{50}{2} \times$10^{-2} \\ & I=2 $\times$9.8 $\times$10^{-3} $\times\left(\frac{50}{2} \times$10^{-2}\right)^2 \\ & I=1225 $\times$10^{-4} $\mathrm{k}-$g^2 m^{-2}=10^{-5} $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{m}$\\ & p=q(2 l)=20 $\times$10^{-6} $\times$50 $\times$10^{-2} \\ & E=121 $\mathrm{~N}$/ $\mathrm{C}$\\ & T=2 $\pi \sqrt{\frac{1225 \times 10^{-4}}{10^{-5} \times 121}}=$2 $\times$3.14 $\times$3.181 \\ & T=19.98 \cong 20 $\mathrm{~s} \end{aligned}$But time taken by the rod to become parallel will be $T / 4$, so required time is $5 \mathrm{~s}$.

questions.q:
Two concentric conducting spheres of radii ${r}_{1}$ and ${\text{r}}_{\text{2}} \left({\text{r}}_{\text{1}}{\text{< r}}_{\text{2}}\right) carry electric charges of $+ Q$ and $- Q$ respectively. The region between the sphere is filled with two insulating layers of dielectric constant ${\text{ε}}_{1}$ and ${\text{ε}}_{2}$ and width ${d}_{1}$ and ${d}_{2}$ respectively. Variation of potential and electric field with radial distance from O is given. Select the correct one. (assume $Vat{r}_{2} = 0$)

$
questions.solution:
Lets take value of Electric field in given regions as${E}_{1}, {E}_{2}, {E}_{3}and{E}_{4}$~respectively.

For~$\text{r} < {r}_{1}\text{,}$~net charge enclosed by the gaussian surface will be zero.
${∴E}_{1} = 0$

For~${r}_{1} < \text{r} < {r}_{1} + \text{d}\text{,}$~from the concept of di-electrics we know that electric field in the presence of dielectric will be reduced by a factor equal to dielectric constant.
$∴ { E}_{2} = \dfrac{Q}{4{πε}_{0}r^{2}{ε}_{1}}$

Same way for~${r}_{1} + \text{d} < \text{r} < { r}_{2}\text{,}$

${E}_{3} = \dfrac{Q}{4{πε}_{0}{ε}_{2}r^{2}}$

Fro~$\text{r} > {r}_{2}\text{,}$~if we draw a spherical gaussian surface, net charge enclosed by it would be zero. Hence electric field outside~${r}_{2}$~distance from the center will be zero.
$∴ {E}_{4} = 0$
Potential is given by~$V = - {∫}_{∞}^{r}\overset{→}{E} . d\overset{→}{r} \ldots \ldots \left(i\right)$
Since electric field is zero outside~${r}_{2}$~and upto infinity so potential will be zero between~${r}_{2}$~and~$\infty .$
i.e. $\text{V} = - \mathop{∫}_{\infty}^{r}\text{E.dr} =0$

Electric field depends on \dfrac{1}{r2}~ between~${r}_{1}to{r}_{2}$, from equation~ \left(i\right)$~potential also varies between~${r}_{1}to{r}_{2}$~and from~${r<r}_{1}$ \text{ and } , electric field is zero. Hence pototential will be constant in that region.

$

questions.q: Consider a solid cube made up of insulating material having a uniform volume charge density. Assuming the electrostatic potential to be zero at infinity, the ratio of the potential at a corner of the cube to that at the centre will be
questions.solution:
$ρ -$Charge density of the cube

${V}_l^{corner} -$ Potential at the corner of a cube of side $l$

${V}_l^{centre} -$ Potential at the centre of a cube of side $l$

${V}_{l / 2}^{centre} -$ Potential at the center of a cube of side $\dfrac{l}{2}$

${V}_{l / 2}^{corner} -$ Potential at the corner of a cube of side $\dfrac{l}{2}$

By dimensional analysis

${V}_l^{corner} ∝ \dfrac{Q}{l} = ρl^{2}$

${V}_l^{corner} = 4{V}_{l / 2}^{corner}$

But by superposition ${V}_l^{centre} = 8{V}_{l / 2}^{corner}$

Because of the centre of the larger cube lies at a corner of the eight smaller cubes of which it is made

Therefore, $\dfrac{{V}_l^{corner}}{{V}_l^{centre}} = \dfrac{4{V}_{l / 2}^{corner}}{8{V}_{l / 2}^{corner}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main
